title: Ava Kingdom
capsule: The Kingdom of Ava (Inwa) was an Irrawaddy Valley state founded in 1364-1365 by Thado Minbya at the confluence of the Irrawaddy and Myitnge rivers, succeeding the earlier Sagaing and Pinya kingdoms to become the dominant power of Upper Burma. Its court engaged in the prolonged Forty Years' War (1385-1424) against the Mon kingdom of Hanthawaddy in Lower Burma and became a major centre of Burmese literature and Theravada Buddhist scholarship. From the late fifteenth century Ava weakened under the pressure of breakaway vassals and the rising Shan states, and in 1527 a Confederation of Shan States led by Mohnyin Thado sacked the city and ended the kingdom's independence, installing puppet rulers and inaugurating a period of Shan domination over Upper Burma.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Core territorial extent is moderately attested through Burmese chronicles (Hmannan Yazawin) and Portuguese accounts, though exact boundaries remain approximate.
